prompt: Create a production-quality planetary surface ALBEDO map for a realistic dry rocky planet in a Unity space game. Landscape 2:1 equirectangular world texture, highest available native resolution. Entire canvas is flat top-down satellite-cartographic terrain, edge to edge. NOT a globe, not a scene, no space, no stars, no text, no atmosphere or sun. Reference image is the target geology and palette only; unwrap its highly detailed dry terrain into a complete new global map. Strongly varied naturally occurring terrain at several scales: a few broad ochre ancient continental plateaus surrounded by dark charcoal basalt plains, huge deeply branching rift canyons with many sharp tributaries, extensive finely folded jagged mountain chains, dense overlapping crater fields mixed with isolated large complex impact craters with central peaks and ejecta, eroded badlands and sedimentary strata. The entire surface must be rich in physically plausible satellite geology, detailed at the scale of a planet photographed from orbit. Avoid soft rounded cellular noise, bubbles, blobs, pebble texture and repetitive shapes. Preserve distinct large features that remain legible when the whole map is reduced to 600 pixels wide. Medium-scale folded ridges and tributaries matter more than tiny grain. Dry muted burnt ochre, rusty mineral deposits, pale sandstone and cold charcoal volcanic rock; no blue, water, ice, snow, clouds or vegetation. Neutral diffuse overhead illumination for a material texture: no directional cast shadows, no highlights or sunlit side, no baked terminator. Moderate albedo, no blown highlights. Horizontally seamless wrap, terrain continues naturally across left and right edges; gently stretched equirectangular poles with no polar ice. Visually comparable to a high-detail real planetary orbiter surface mosaic.
